Order 
In this petition the petitioners are seeking grant of bail for the offences punishable under Sections 506,504, 406, 420, 34 of IPC, in Crime No.263/2023 of Nelamangala Police.

2. Heard the arguments of Sri. Babu. M. Rao., learned counsel for the petitioners and Smt. Sowmya.
R., learned High Court Government Pleader.
3.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the brother of the complainant, it is he who helping the complainant in all aspects.
Some financial transactions in the year 2007 and 2009 were already return to the complainant.
Due to mis- understanding complaint has been filed.
The matter will be NC: 2023:KHC:37719 settled between the brother and sister amicably, the Petitioners are ready to abide any conditions sought for grant of bail.

4. Per contra, learned learned High Court Government Pleader has contended that, the complainant arranged a sum of Rs.8,80,000/- in the year 2007 and Rs.20,20,000/- in the year 2009 was paid to the accused No.1.
The accused No.1 received the said money with a promise of enrichment of his sister.
He did not enrich her nor returned the money and thereby committed cheating and breach of trust.
When she demanded return she was abused and threatened forcing her to file the complaint.
If bail is granted the petitioners will threatened the complainant, tamper the evidence.
5. I gave my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and perused the materials on record.
6. It is an un-fortunate case where sister making allegation against her own brother that she has been cheated by him to a tune of Rs.30,00,000/-.

The material on record also point out that money Sri Krishna Murthy vs State Of Karnataka on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163833610/
2 so paid was in the years 2007 and 2009 whereas demanded for repayment was made in the year 2023.

sentences.text: Between 2009 to 2023 what was transferred between brother NC: 2023:KHC:37719 and sister is not forthcoming in the complaint.
The allegation against the accused No.1 that he has received the money from the complainant to make her financially rich but it was not materialized.
Brother telling his sister that he could not refund the money due to loss suffered in the business on which the money of his sister was invested.
The matter required investigation result of the same will unearth the fate of Rs.30,00,000/- paid by the complainant to her brother.
At this stage I do not find Prima-facie material against the petitioners.
7. The accused Nos.3 and 4 are the children of the petitioner were granted bail by the Learned Sessions Judge in Criminal.

8. Having regard to the gravity of the offence punishment prescribed and also the relationship between the parties, I do not found any reasons to refuse exercise of discretion in favour of the petitioners.
The petitioners have come forward to assist for the investigation and abide all the conditions that would be imposed against them by this Court.
Hence, there is no reason to refuse exercise of discretion in favour of the petitioners.

Conditions will meet the apprehension NC:
2023:KHC:37719 of the prosecution.
Hence the petition deserves merit consideration.

In the result, the following;
ORDER (i) The Petition is allowed.

(ii) The petitioners are ordered to be released on bail in the event of their arrest in Crime No.263/2023 registered by the Nelamangala Police for the offence punishable under Sections 506,
504, 406, 420 and 34 of IPC, on execution of a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one like bond to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer.
